set.body:
Phase B (assurance floor; gates Phase F).

Current state: project/Dependencies.scala:5 pins scala3 = "3.7.4"; build.sbt:11 has crossScalaVersions := Seq(Versions.scala3) — ONE entry; .github/workflows/ci.yml:31 has scala: [3] — ONE matrix entry. Matrix breadth comes only from Java (temurin 17 + 21) on a single OS (ubuntu-22.04).

Why it matters: a compiler consumes compatible TASTy from the same or an EARLIER minor line, so publishing from 3.7 excludes every 3.3 LTS consumer. Scala explicitly recommends publishing libraries on the LTS line. 3.8.4 is the current regular release; 3.3.8 the current LTS.

CORRECTION TO THE REVIEW's sbt mechanics: because Scala 3 versions share _3 artifact coordinates, a careless +publish across 3.3.8 and 3.8.4 attempts the same artifact twice. Therefore:
- default and release publication from 3.3.8 ONLY;
- explicit TEST lanes for both 3.3.8 and 3.8.4;
- release tooling publishes only the default line.

Do this in Phase B rather than Phase F: it surfaces LTS compile errors while the API is still moving and they are cheap to fix, instead of after Phase D when they are not. ADR 0001 states that changing the Scala minor line is an explicit compatibility decision — this bead IS that decision and must update the ADR.

Acceptance: green test lanes on 3.3.8 and 3.8.4; publishLocal produces _3 artifacts from 3.3.8 only.
set.title: P8.B4: Scala 3.3.8 publication baseline and 3.8.4 test lane
